title: Inspect and extend: Share browser state across screens
objective: Use the real implementation in `Sources/ContentView.swift` to demonstrate and safely improve observable store lifecycle, tab navigation, and settings binding.
problem: A shared store lets multiple screens show the same browser state. Trace initialization and environment injection before following a tap into a state-changing method. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `Sources/ContentView.swift` and the related project files: Sources/ContentView.swift; Sources/Screens/TabsView.swift; Sources/Screens/HomeView.swift; Sources/Screens/SettingsView.swift.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to observable store lifecycle, tab navigation, and settings binding.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: Account sync, history sync, and production data management are not implemented.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: A shared store lets multiple screens show the same browser state. Trace initialization and environment injection before following a tap into a state-changing method.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `Sources/ContentView.swift`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
